# runr_private_connection (Resource)

A private connection of a project to a managed PostgreSQL database through Skupper ([private database connections](https://runr.sh/docs/environments/#private-database-connections)): a Skupper Link, a Listener and a credentials Secret in the project namespace of the region the workload runs in. The project's own workload, or with `environment` one of its environments, gets `<env_prefix>DATABASE_URL`, `<env_prefix>PGHOST`, … (`env_names`); the running workload gets them at once, else with its next deploy. The region must run Skupper v2; global projects cannot have private connections.

The credentials (`link_token`, `database`, `username`, `password`) live in the region only and never come back from the API: Terraform keeps what it set (the token and the password sensitive), or with `link_token_wo` / `password_wo` (Terraform 1.11 and later) no token and password at all — change `credentials_wo_version` to connect with new ones. RunR cannot change a connection: changing any argument replaces it (its workload is without the connection in between). Needs `connections.manage` on the project. Import with `<project name or id>/<connection name or id>` (the project's own workload) or `<project name or id>/<environment>/<connection name or id>`; the credentials are not imported, the next apply takes the configured ones into the state without replacing the connection.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# production reaches its managed PostgreSQL privately: ORDERS_DATABASE_URL, ORDERS_PGHOST, …
resource "runr_private_connection" "orders" {
  project_id  = runr_project.api.id
  name        = "orders"
  env_prefix  = "ORDERS_"
  routing_key = "pg-orders"
  link_token  = file("${path.module}/orders-access-token.yaml") # the Skupper v2 AccessToken of the database's site
  database    = "orders"
  username    = "orders_app"
  password    = var.orders_password
}

# staging reaches its own database, never production's. Terraform 1.11 and later: the token and
# the password stay out of the state; bump credentials_wo_version to connect with new ones.
resource "runr_private_connection" "orders_staging" {
  project_id             = runr_project.api.id
  environment            = runr_environment.staging.name
  name                   = "orders"
  env_prefix             = "ORDERS_"
  routing_key            = "pg-orders-staging"
  link_token_wo          = var.orders_staging_token
  database               = "orders"
  username               = "orders_app"
  password_wo            = var.orders_staging_password
  credentials_wo_version = "1"
}

output "orders_connection" {
  value = { host = runr_private_connection.orders.host, status = runr_private_connection.orders.status }
}

variable "orders_password" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
}

variable "orders_staging_token" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
  ephemeral = true
}

variable "orders_staging_password" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
  ephemeral = true
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `database` (String) Database name.
- `name` (String) Name, unique per workload (at most 30 characters).
- `project_id` (String) Project id.
- `routing_key` (String) Skupper routing key of the database's connector.
- `username` (String) Database user.

### Optional

> **NOTE**: [Write-only arguments](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments) are supported in Terraform 1.11 and later.

- `credentials_wo_version` (String) Any string; a change replaces the connection with the current `link_token_wo` / `password_wo`.
- `env_prefix` (String) Prefix of the variable names, e.g. `ORDERS_` (default none); unique per workload.
- `environment` (String) Environment the connection belongs to (`runr_environment.<name>.name` or its id); its connection lives in the region that environment runs in, and only its workload gets the variables. Left out (or `production`): the project's own workload.
- `link_token` (String, Sensitive) The Skupper v2 AccessToken, or Link with its TLS Secret (YAML), the database's site issued. One of `link_token` and `link_token_wo` is required.
- `link_token_wo` (String, Sensitive, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) `link_token` that Terraform never stores (write-only, Terraform 1.11 and later); change `credentials_wo_version` to use a new one.
- `password` (String, Sensitive) Password of the database user (sensitive). One of `password` and `password_wo` is required.
- `password_wo` (String, Sensitive, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) `password` that Terraform never stores (write-only, Terraform 1.11 and later); change `credentials_wo_version` to use a new one.
- `port` (Number) Port of the local listener (default `5432`).
- `sslmode` (String) PostgreSQL `sslmode` of the connection (default `require`).

### Read-Only

- `env_names` (List of String) The variables the workload gets.
- `host` (String) Host name the functions connect to (the Listener's Service).
- `id` (String) Connection id.
- `link_kind` (String) `access_token` (redeemed into a Link by Skupper) or `link`.
- `resource_name` (String) Name of its Skupper Link and Listener in the region (`<name>-<suffix>`).
- `secret_name` (String) The credentials Secret in the region.
- `status` (String) What the region reports: `ready`, `pending` or `error` (read with every refresh).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# <project name or id>/<connection name or id> (the project's own workload)
terraform import runr_private_connection.orders orders-api/orders

# <project name or id>/<environment>/<connection name or id>. The credentials are not imported:
# the next apply takes the configured ones into the state without replacing the connection.
terraform import runr_private_connection.orders_staging orders-api/staging/orders
```
